newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Danish police investigating UNICEF employee.
newsitem.headline: Danish police investigating UNICEF employee.

text.p: UNICEF, the U.N. Children's Fund, on Monday accused an employee in its Copenhagen office of procuring about $500,000 worth of supplies for the agency from a Swedish company in which he had a financial interest.
The employee, whose nationality was said to be Norwegian, worked in UNICEF's supply division office in Copenhagen and Danish prosecutors were investigating the case.

The staff member, dismissed, worked for UNICEF for 10 years. According to a statement by the agency he had a "financial interest" in a Swedish company with which UNICEF had done $500,000 worth of business since 1993.

The irregularities were discovered during a UNICEF audit of the Copenhagen office in May and were followed up by the U.N. Office of Internal Oversight Services, which serves as the U.N. inspector-general.
In turning the case over to Denmark's Public Prosecutor's Office for Serious Economic Crimes, UNICEF said it waived the employee's diplomatic immunity.
Emily Booker, spokeswoman for the agency, said the name of the staff member could not be released while the Danish authorities investigated.

UNICEF's supply division in Copenhagen procures goods for the agency as well as other aid organisations, including materials for education, immunisation, health, nutrition, transport and water and sanitation programmes. Costs of these supplies amounted to $278 million in 1995.

In Copenhagen Veronica Li Frankenstein, the newly appointed director of the supply division, said, "We are obviously extremely disturbed that an employee appears to have used his position to further his own private interests."
"But at the same time I am encouraged that it was our own audit investigation that exposed the situation," she said.
Sources said the suspect was a Norwegian who held a middle management position in the agency's supply division.
